Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Marcus Hale, CFO; Dr. Lena Kim, Chief Manufacturing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q2 2024 was a strong quarter for Voltara Motors. We made significant progress in several key areas, including ramping production volumes while optimizing capacity utilization, expanding gross margins per vehicle through cost efficiencies, advancing our strategic priorities for scalable growth, maintaining resilient average selling prices across models and regions, and achieving robust total vehicle deliveries. The demand for our next-generation EV platforms continues to be strong, and we are working diligently to increase production capacity to meet that demand. The impact of our vertically integrated battery and manufacturing innovations is exceeding our initial expectations.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. Good morning, everyone. For Q2 2024, our revenue was $13.1 billion, representing a 35% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 22%, reflecting our ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency and per-vehicle economics. Our operating expenses were $1.8 billion, and net income was $850 million. We continue to maintain a healthy balance sheet with $5.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our guidance for the next quarter is revenue of $15 to $16 billion, with gross margins expanding to 23-24% and deliveries in the 280,000 to 300,000 range.

Before moving on, let me provide more color on some of these key metrics starting with our total vehicle deliveries volume. In Q2, we delivered a record 248,700 vehicles globally, up 47% year-over-year from 169,200 units in the prior year and 12% sequentially from Q1's 221,900. This momentum reflects accelerating execution on our EV transition strategy, fueled by ramps at our Fremont, Shanghai, and Texas Gigafactories, alongside sustained demand for our Spark sedan, Terra SUV, Titan pickup, and emerging Urban hatchback platforms, all supported by IRA incentives and easing interest rates.

By model, the Spark sedan led with 142,500 deliveries, a 52% YoY jump, now at 57% of our mix thanks to its 800V architecture, LFP packs from in-house production, and a refreshed $32,900 starting price with 320-mile EPA range after OTA efficiency gains. The Terra SUV followed with 65,200 units, up 42% YoY, driven by high take-rates on the 100 kWh structural pack for over 400 miles of range and Level 3 autonomy approvals in key U.S. states. Our Titan pickup hit 41,000 deliveries, 38% higher YoY, with Giga Texas exceeding 1,200 units daily by quarter-end, appealing to fleets like logistics giants via its exoskeleton durability. The Apex hypercar added 50 units to early adopters, prepping for volume.

Regionally, North America took 45% at 112,400 units, up 55% YoY and grabbing 18% U.S. EV share per Cox data, thanks to $7,500 IRA rebates and 15% BOM cost cuts. China delivered 78,900 or 32%, growing 40% YoY from Shanghai's 95% utilization despite BYD competition. Europe hit 52,400 or 21%, surging 62% on subsidies though tariffs nicked ASPs. RoW added 5,000 via pilots in Australia and Mexico.

Retail orders rose 22% QoQ with inventory at just 12 days, beating benchmarks. Dry electrode 4680s boosted density by 30%, FSD v12.5 rolled to 65% of fleet for better resale, and Q3 production of 255,000 drove 21.5% margins up 320 bps. With $2.5 billion CapEx including Berlin Phase 2, we're set for Q4's 280k-300k deliveries and 20%+ share gains in 2025 per BloombergNEF.

Shifting to production volume and capacity utilization rates, these numbers highlight our vertical integration and scaling prowess in a market with softening demand pockets, post-4680 ramp issues, and competition from GM Ultium and Ford Lightning. Production hit 248,000 vehicles, 28% YoY growth from 193,000 and 12% sequential from 221,000, beating our 235k-245k guide. Battery output was 18.2 GWh, up 35% YoY, hitting 95% vertical integration for LFP and NMC.

Model breakdown: Model S sedan at 72,000 units, up 15% YoY, 92% utilization for fleet demand offsetting Europe retail softness. Model X SUV, our hero at 105,000 or 42% of total, ramped 45% YoY post-4680 quals, with structural packs cutting BOM 18%. CyberVolt pickup at 52,000, doubling from 28,000, 21% mix from Texas at 4.2 weeks inventory vs. industry 6.5. Model 2 hatchback piloted 19,000 from Reno for $25k mass-market vs. BYD Seagull.

Utilization averaged 87% on 1.2 million run-rate, up 510 bps QoQ. Fremont: 112k vehicles/7.8 GWh on 650k/50 GWh capacity at 92%, +650 bps YoY with AI robotics at 9.5-hour cycles. Shanghai: 85k/6.5 GWh on 400k/60 GWh at 95%, +1,200 bps via local LFP. Texas: 38k/2.9 GWh on 250k/25 GWh at 78%, new ramp. Berlin: 13k/1 GWh on 200k/20 GWh at 65%, -200 bps on regs, idling for prismatic cells.

Supply chains normalized with TSMC semis at 100%, unwinding air premiums. Unboxed process targets 25% CapEx savings by 2025, 98% cell yields. Q3 guide: 280k-300k at 90-92% utilization, front-loading CyberVolt/Model 2 for IRA stability. 2026: 2.5M at 95%+ via India-Tata JV for APAC 25% share. This discipline eyes 25-30% FCF margins by 2026.

Next, gross margin per vehicle, a core profitability gauge: ASP minus COGS per unit. We hit $14,200, or 18% on 248,700 deliveries—wait, aligning with our overall 22% gross—up 22% YoY from $11,600 and 8% QoQ from $13,150, ahead of Rivian's ~$10k, nearing Tesla's $16.5k Model mix.

COGS dropped to $42,800, -7.4% YoY: Batteries (40% COGS) at $85/kWh via Nevada 46-series dry electrode/silicon anodes, saving $1,800/vehicle toward $70/kWh YE. Efficiencies at 92% utilization, Gigapress cut BIW 60% SKUs/15% costs ($900 save), structural packs to 180 Wh/kg. Supply tailwinds stabilized nickel/LFP, avoiding $400 hits.

ASP steady $57,000 on 65% high-margin Model X ($68k, $18.5k margin), 20% premium sedans vs. 15%/45% last year; BoltMax-like entry at 15%. NA: $15,400 (75% vol) on 65% IRA content/$7.5k credits/35% F&A. Europe: $12,800 on price wars. China/APAC: $13,500 nascent with software premiums.

Pathfinder 2.0 for Q1'25 targets $20k+ margins via unboxed/50% parts cut, OTA subs $99/mo (25% attach), V2G $2k LTV. Vs. legacy 8-12%, we eye 25% by 2026 at 500k run-rate. Q3: $14,800-$15,200 on 280k+.

Finally, ASP trends by model/region show pricing power: Global $52,800, +4% YoY flat QoQ on premium shift. Deliveries 248k mix: 42% sedans, 35% SUVs, 18% pickups, 5% Urban.

Spark: $41,200 -3% YoY on RWD fleets but +2% QoQ via $4.5k Autopilot, 22% margins/LFP. Trailblazer SUV (Model X equiv): $68,400 +7% on 4680/Adventure Pack. Titan (CyberVolt): $82,500 +12% on gigacasting/800V/V2G, CARB credits. Urban: $28,900 debut.

Regions: NA 45% $64,200 +8% IRA/Tesla alt. China 30% $38,500 -2% wars/incentives. Europe 18% $55,800 +3% subsidies/Berlin. RoW 7% $49,300 +6% AUS/India.

NA share +2 pts despite fleets. China tiered pricing, 4680 Q4. Europe regs/FX hedge. Battery $85/kWh, FSD 35% attach $1.2k ARPU, 40% in-house. Q3 $53,500 +1% on Titan ramp. 5-7% CAGR to 2027 on $60k+ mix.

I'll now turn the call over to Dr. Lena Kim to provide an update on our manufacturing operations.

Dr. Lena Kim:
Thank you, Marcus. We are pleased with the progress we've made in scaling up production of our next-gen platforms like the CyberVolt and Model 2. Building on the production details Marcus shared, our Fremont and Shanghai facilities are operating near peak with AI-driven automation and localized sourcing mitigating tariffs. Texas is ramping deliberately to 85% in Q3 with Panasonic 4680 dry-electrode quals for 16% density gains, while Berlin retooled lines prioritize U.S./China output. Initiatives like Unboxed manufacturing and 98% cell yields are reducing cycle times and CapEx, keeping us lean at 3.8-week inventories vs. industry bloat. We're on track to meet our production targets for the year and beyond, positioning for that 2.5 million 2026 goal.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw, star two. Our first question comes from Jordan Lee with Goldman Sachs.

Analyst 1:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On production utilization, Berlin was a bit soft at 65%—can you elaborate on the retooling timeline and any impact on Europe deliveries?

Dr. Lena Kim:
Great question, Jordan. Berlin's 65% reflects temporary idling of one Model X line for prismatic cell integration and ADAS regulatory holds, down 200 bps YoY amid subsidy cuts. Retooling wraps by late Q3, targeting 85% utilization and 20k+ Q4 deliveries. We're prioritizing higher-ASP U.S./China but expect Europe rebound with two more models qualifying for €4k incentives, adding localized sourcing savings.

Operator:
Next from Emily Chen at Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 2:
Marcus, your gross margin per vehicle guidance implies nice expansion—how much is tied to mix vs. cost-downs, and any risks if entry-level volumes pick up?

Marcus Hale:
Emily, spot on. Of the $14,800-$15,200 Q3 target, about 60% from cost-downs like $70/kWh batteries and Gigapress, 40% mix favoring Model X/Titan at 53% combined. Entry-level like Model 2 at 15% mix prioritizes 20% margins via sodium-ion; if it scales to 20-25%, we'd still hit 23% overall thanks to Pathfinder 2.0's 50% parts reduction. Risks like commodities are derisked by our $2.5B program.

Operator:
From Raj Patel at JPMorgan.

Analyst 3:
Lena, on capacity, what's the latest on Texas Gigafactory ramp for CyberVolt and any bottlenecks remaining post-4680 quals?

Dr. Lena Kim:
Raj, Texas is pacing beautifully at 78% now, with Q3 to 85% as Panasonic dry-electrode hits volume—promising 16% density for 500-mile range. Semicon normalization to 100% unwound prior premiums; Unboxed process is live, cutting CapEx 25% by '25. Bottlenecks minimal—dealer inventory at 4.2 weeks—we're aligned with IRA incentives.

Operator:
From Sarah Kline at Barclays.

Analyst 4:
Elena, your strategic priorities mention autonomy rollout—can you update on NovaVolt OS timelines and monetization potential?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Sarah. Q4 priorities include flawless NVX ramp to 110k-120k deliveries, $2.8B-$3B revenue at 24-25% margins. For 2025, $14-16B revenue, 12-15% EBITDA on portfolio expansion: NVX Pickup Q1 (500-mile/11k lb tow), NVZ sedan Q2 Europe, sub-$30k NV1 Q3 India/APAC. Autonomy: OS 2.0 Q1 with 2.5B miles training, unsupervised FSD Beta Q2 at $99/mo for $400M recurring. Mobileye/NVIDIA partnerships fast-track robotaxis. This compounds our 28% cost edge for 20% U.S. premium share by 2027.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Operator:
From Mike Torres at Citi.

Analyst 5:
Marcus, ASP held resilient—thoughts on China pressure and how software offsets?

Marcus Hale:
Mike, China ASP at $38.5k dipped 2% on wars but offset by 20% volume via Shanghai ramp and tiered pricing—premium LR at $48k. Software like neural-net ADAS at 35% attach adds $1.2k ARPU recurring. Q3 $53.5k global on Titan ramp, with CATL JV 4680s recovering +5%. Long-term 5-7% CAGR as 60% mix hits $60k+.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. To wrap with our strategic outlook: Q4 guides 110k-120k deliveries for 480k-520k FY24, revenue $2.8B-$3B. 2025 $14-16B at 25% CAGR, $4.2B CapEx for Mexico Giga/SiC. Priorities: expand to pickups/SUVs/entry, OS 2.0 FSD subs, resilient supply with Redwood recycling/sodium-ion, regional tailwinds like IRA/CHIPS/EU CO2/V2G/China JVs. Headwinds like inventory/Europe demand met by $5.2B liquidity/$500M buybacks. We're confident in executing for shareholder value amid $1T EV TAM.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q2 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
